analysis: Examined base_text of ClusterOnboardingLive.swift (lines 1-911) plus the truncated patch excerpt. The visible changes are: new closures stopsAsked and serveUnlessStopped wired in live() (head 77-78); execute() refactored so the status reply goes through followerStatus(), which adds start progress and a stopsAsked count (head 399-408); and forwarded .serve now passes request.stopsBefore to localServe(unlessStoppedSince:). The patch excerpt is truncated and the head text was not supplied, so the implementations of stopsAsked, currentStopsAsked, serve(unlessStoppedSince:), and the later changed ranges (head 1459+, 2238+, 2377+, 2409+, 2542+, 2573+) were not visible and not reviewed. The visible behavior adds a status field and a serve guard on the existing authenticated link control channel. Forwarded commands go through command() and the pairing link key; the base code already treats the channel as authenticated by the setup exchange. I found no change to the key, attestation, authorization, or coordinator boundaries. The stopsAsked count and stopsBefore value come from the paired peer, so they are not new unauthenticated surface; the peer is already trusted to forward stop and serve, per the base execute() flow. Relevant threat IDs (none of which this PR evidently touches) include TB-013/TB-014, T-059, and T-062 for local command and root boundaries. Open questions for integration: whether the stop-versus-serve race guard fails closed; whether the stopsBefore comparison can be forged or replayed to suppress a person's stop request or to restart serving after a stop; and whether the new counter is persisted safely in the ClusterSetupRecord (the owner-only store). The rest of the file's changes need review once head text is available.
